message.content:
Build a **Mailbox Settings** experience for the native Nxeon mail client in /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 + Prisma + Tailwind, dark-navy/violet theme). Inspiration: Titan Mail / Zoho mailbox settings — but cleaner and on-brand. Read first: `lib/actions-mail.ts` (patterns, `resolveMailbox` from `lib/mail/imap.ts`, rate limits), `lib/mailcow.ts` (existing Mailcow API client — MAILCOW_API_URL already ends in `/api/v1`, do NOT double it; there's already `mcSetMailboxPassword`), `components/customer/mail/*` (esp. `FolderRail.tsx` which has a "Mail settings" Tools link that's currently inert, and `Composer.tsx`), `app/dashboard/mail/page.tsx`, and the Prisma `Mailbox` model (new fields: `signature String?`, `displayName String?`, `autoReplyEnabled Boolean @default(false)`, `autoReplySubject String?`, `autoReplyBody String?`). Do NOT touch prisma/schema.prisma (fields exist). Do NOT run git.

ONLY edit: `lib/actions-mail.ts` (or add `lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts`), `lib/mailcow.ts`, and files under `components/customer/mail/` + `app/dashboard/mail/`.

Build a settings panel (a modal or a routed `/dashboard/mail/settings` view — pick the cleaner fit; wire the existing "Mail settings" link in FolderRail to open it) with these sections, all owner/ownership-checked via `resolveMailbox` and rate-limited on writes:

1. **Identity & signature** — `displayName` + a `signature` (textarea, plain text or light HTML). Stored on the Mailbox row via a new `saveMailboxSettings` action. **Apply the signature in the Composer** (`components/customer/mail/Composer.tsx`): when composing a NEW message, prefill the body with the signature (below a separator); for replies, append it below the quote. Load the signature into the mail page's props.
2. **Connection details** — a read-only, copyable panel for setting up external mail apps (Outlook/Apple Mail/Thunderbird): IMAP `mail.nxeon.cloud` port 993 SSL/TLS; SMTP `mail.nxeon.cloud` port 587 STARTTLS; username = the full mailbox address; "use your mailbox password". Each value has a copy button. This is the Titan/Zoho "configure your device" section.
3. **Aliases** — list/add/remove email aliases for the mailbox's domain via Mailcow. Add `mcListAliases(domain)`, `mcAddAlias(address, goto)`, `mcDeleteAlias(id)` to `lib/mailcow.ts` (Mailcow endpoints: `GET /get/alias/all/<domain>`, `POST /add/alias` with `{address, goto, active:"1"}`, `POST /delete/alias` with `[id]`). Actions `listAliases()`, `addAlias(alias, goto?)`, `removeAlias(id)` — validate the alias is on a domain the user owns (check their EmailSubscription domains); default `goto` = the mailbox itself. UI to manage them.
4. **Auto-reply / vacation responder** — toggle + subject + message, stored on the Mailbox row (`autoReply*`). Attempt to apply it on the mail server if the Mailcow API supports it (research briefly — Mailcow has no simple vacation API in most builds; if you can't reliably set it server-side, STILL store it in the DB and clearly label the UI "Auto-reply is saved; server-side delivery of auto-replies is rolling out" rather than pretending it sends). Do not claim it works if it doesn't.
5. **Change password** — reuse the existing `resetMailboxPassword` action (shows the new password once) — surface it here too.

Match the mail client's quality bar and the Nxeon design system (reuse `card`/`input`/`label`/`btn-*`/`section-label`, existing icons). Handle loading/empty/error states; every write returns a clear `{ok,error}` or throws with a friendly message.

IMPORTANT: `Write`/`Edit` tools may intermittently time out on a PreToolUse hook — if so, fall back to `Bash` heredocs and verify files exist. Do NOT run `npm run build`/`next build`. Verify ONLY with `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v "test/.*test.ts"` (clean for your files). Report the actions added, the Mailcow endpoints used, how the signature is applied in Composer, and — honestly — whether auto-reply actually sends server-side or is store-only.

content.thinking:
I'm settling on a structure: a separate server action file for settings to keep things organized, and a modal component for the UI that follows the same pattern as the Composer. The task description seems to cut off mid-sentence, but the core approach is clear.

For the modal, I'll add an `onOpenSettings` callback to FolderRail instead of using the `<a href>`, so it opens within MailClient and preserves the active mailbox context. Then I'll define the server actions to fetch and update mailbox settings from the database, using the mailbox resolution logic to verify ownership.

Since Mailcow doesn't expose a reliable auto-reply API, I'll store auto-reply settings locally in the database and be transparent about that limitation. I also need to fetch the full mailbox row to access signature and other settings fields that `resolveMailbox` doesn't return.

For aliases, I'll list all aliases on the domain that the user owns (verified via EmailSubscription), returning their id, address, goto, and active status. When adding an alias, I'll validate it's on a domain the user owns, default the goto to the mailbox itself if not specified, apply rate-limiting, and call the Mailcow API.

For removing an alias, I need to fetch the alias list, verify it belongs to a domain the user owns, then delete it. For password resets, I can reuse the existing resetMailboxPassword function but need to wrap it so the client-side modal can pass the mailbox address instead of the ID — I'll create a settings action that resolves the address to an ID server-side and calls the underlying logic.

There's a potential issue though: resolveMailbox requires an already-decryptable password and throws if none exists, which creates a chicken-and-egg problem for the reset flow. But since the mail settings context assumes the user is already authenticated with a working password (resolveMailbox is used throughout), this should be fine in practice.

Now I'm mapping out the Mailcow alias API functions: listing all aliases for a domain, adding new aliases with address and forwarding target, and deleting aliases by ID.

I need to define a type for the alias objects returned from Mailcow, then handle domain validation by checking if the alias domain matches one of the user's owned domains from their EmailSubscriptions. For the add alias function, I'll accept either a full email address or just the local part, defaulting to the mailbox's domain if needed.

For the page setup, I'll fetch the mailbox settings in page.tsx and pass the signature and display name to the MailClient component. Since the active mailbox can change, I'll store settings in MailClient's state and refetch whenever the user switches mailboxes, so the composer always uses the correct signature for the current mailbox.

For the separator between the message body and signature, I'm using the RFC 3676 standard format...

Now I'm thinking through how the signature placement works differently depending on the message type. For a new message, I can just prepend the signature to the body with the delimiter, and it's straightforward since the user can edit it. But for replies and forwards, the signature needs to appear below the quoted text, which is trickier since the composer currently builds the HTML by escaping the plaintext body first, then appending the quoted HTML as a blockquote. That means the signature text would end up above the quote instead of below it. I need to rethink the composer structure to handle this properly.

The cleanest approach is to pass the signature as a separate optional parameter to the Composer, then have the submit function build the HTML in the right order: the user's reply body, then the blockquote with the quoted text, then the signature appended at the end. For the plaintext version, I'd append the signature after the body as well. For new mode the signature goes directly into the body with a separator so it's editable, while for replies and forwards I'll pass it separately in the draft and have Composer append it after the quote. In the submit method, I need to handle building the signature block differently depending on the mode—for text payloads it's straightforward since the quote only appears in HTML, but for HTML I need to figure out where exactly to insert it.

Now I'm thinking through how to handle the signature content itself. The task specifies it can be plain text or light HTML, but I need to decide whether to escape it in the Composer for safety or preserve any HTML formatting. Injecting raw HTML into the composed message is safe since it's the user's own content being sent via SMTP, not rendered in our app, so there's no meaningful XSS risk. But malformed HTML could break the layout, so I'm leaning toward treating the signature as plain text in the composer—escaping special characters and converting newlines to preserve predictability. I'll document that the "light HTML" allowance in storage is currently applied as plain text for safety.

For the Composer implementation, I'm adding a `signature` field to ComposeDraft and updating the submit method to escape the signature, build both text and HTML blocks with proper formatting, and append them according to whether it's a new message or a reply. Writing the mailcow integration...

content.text:
Done. Everything type-checks clean (`npx tsc --noEmit` produced no output for any of the touched files) and no schema or git changes were made. ## What was built A **Mailbox Settings** modal for the native webmail client, opened from the previously-inert "Mail settings" link in `FolderRail`. Implemented as a modal (not a route) because it keeps the active-mailbox context and matches the existing Composer overlay pattern. It has a Titan/Zoho-style left section rail with five sections, all owner-checked via `resolveMailbox` and rate-limited on writes. ### Files - **`lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts`** (new) — all settings server actions. - **`lib/mailcow.ts`** — added alias client functions + `MailcowAlias` type. - **`components/customer/mail/MailSettings.tsx`** (new) — the modal UI. - **`components/customer/mail/FolderRail.tsx`** — "Mail settings" `` → button with `onOpenSettings`. - **`components/customer/mail/Composer.tsx`** — signature support in `ComposeDraft` + outgoing body. - **`components/customer/mail/MailClient.tsx`** — signature state, settings modal wiring, per-mailbox signature refresh on switch. - **`app/dashboard/mail/page.tsx`** — loads the default mailbox's signature into props. ### Server actions added (`lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts`) - `getMailboxSettings(addr?)` — reads DB row (displayName/signature/autoReply*). - `saveMailboxSettings({displayName, signature}, addr?)` — identity + signature, validated + rate-limited. - `saveAutoReply({enabled, subject, body}, addr?)` — **store-only** (see below). - `listAliases(addr?)`, `addAlias(alias, goto?, addr?)`, `removeAlias(id, addr?)` — domain-ownership validated against the user's `EmailSubscription.domainName` set; `addAlias` accepts a bare local part (assumes the mailbox domain) and defaults `goto` to the mailbox itself; `removeAlias` re-confirms the alias lives on an owned domain before deleting. - `resetPassword(addr?)` — thin wrapper that resolves ownership then delegates to the existing `resetMailboxPassword(mailboxId)`, surfacing the new password once. ### Mailcow endpoints used (added to `lib/mailcow.ts`) - `mcListAliases(domain)` → `GET /get/alias/all/` - `mcAddAlias(address, goto)` → `POST /add/alias` `{address, goto, active:"1"}` - `mcDeleteAlias(id)` → `POST /delete/alias` `[id]` All go through the existing `mcRequest` (which already handles the `/api/v1` base without doubling it and surfaces `{type:"danger"}` payloads). ### How the signature is applied in the Composer The mailbox signature is loaded into the mail page props → `MailClient` state (refreshed on mailbox switch and after a save). - **New message:** `openCompose` prefills the editable body with `\n\n-- \n{signature}` (below the standard `-- ` separator). - **Reply / forward:** the signature is passed on the draft and `Composer.submit()` appends it **below the quoted original** — as `\n\n-- \n{sig}` in the text part and a styled `--
{sig}` block after the blockquote in the HTML part. The signature is HTML-escaped (applied as plain text) for safe outgoing markup. ### Auto-reply: honest status **Store-only.** Mailcow's REST API exposes no reliable vacation/auto-responder endpoint (auto-replies live in SOGo user preferences, not the admin API), so `saveAutoReply` only persists to the Mailbox row and **does not** send anything server-side. The UI carries an amber notice: "Auto-reply is saved… Server-side delivery of auto-replies is rolling out — until then, these settings are stored but not yet sent automatically." No code claims or attempts actual delivery. ### Connection details Read-only copyable panel: IMAP `mail.nxeon.cloud:993` SSL/TLS, SMTP `mail.nxeon.cloud:587` STARTTLS, username = full mailbox address, with a "use your mailbox password" note. Each value has a copy button (clipboard with copied-check feedback). Loading/empty/error states are handled throughout (skeletons, error notes, empty-alias note, optimistic alias removal with reload-on-failure). Uses the existing `card`/`input`/`label`/`btn-*`/`section-label`/`glass`/`skeleton` classes and the mail `Icon` set. Two notes for you: I did **not** touch `DOCUMENTATION.md` (your memory asks to keep it current, but the task restricted edits to the mail files) — you may want to document this feature there separately. And auto-reply will need a real SOGo-side mechanism if you want it to actually send.
